A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research lineage, with matching HLUQ/CAG methods and COCO baseline results despite the framework's renaming and extension. Text, equations, figures, and tables support comparison. Inspection includes v2's Supplementary Material A-G; v4 ends with references and biographies and contains no separate appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original COCO segmentation experiments, component ablations, FPGA measurements, and supplementary ImageNet classification, sensitivity, and weight-grouping results.

after.justification: v4 reports original COCO and SAM2 video-segmentation results, quantization ablations, weight-conditioning analyses, and FPGA measurements.

M1.justification: AHCQ-SAM retains HLUQ and the iterative clustering procedure of CAG but adds two substantive components: activation-aware proximal weight conditioning with spectral preservation (ACNR), and layer-specific logarithmic quantization of attention scores (LNQ). These change weight preprocessing and post-Softmax quantization, beyond the framework's renaming.

E1.justification: COCO instance segmentation with four prompt detectors remains. v4 adds video object segmentation on DAVIS and SA-V using SAM2, introducing temporal inputs and video segmentation requirements. Conversely, the ImageNet image-classification evaluation on DeiT in v2 Appendix D disappears.

E2.justification: BRECQ, QDrop, and PTQ4SAM remain the main SAM comparators and are reused for SAM2. However, the broader ImageNet comparison against methods including FQ-ViT, APQ-ViT, RepQ-ViT, and I&S-ViT disappears. v4 adds direct comparison with CondiQuant in Figure 12 and explicit AGQ/HLUQ alternatives in the post-Softmax quantizer comparison in Figure 9b.

E3.justification: The calibration specification changes from MinMax initialization to RMSE for weights, retaining MinMax for activations. Component ablations change from W4A4 with YOLOX/H-DETR to W5A5 with Faster R-CNN; other ablations also switch detectors. New video experiments introduce eight-video calibration and J&F evaluation. Hardware validation changes from a decoder MLP block on a 200 MHz Artix FPGA to SAM-B on a 300 MHz ZCU102, adding frame-rate reporting.

E4.justification: v4 rebuilds component ablations around four components, adds attention-quantizer and ACNR-versus-CondiQuant analyses, and replaces qualitative examples. Group-count and post-GELU quantizer investigations remain under revised settings. v2 Appendix A's additional layer-distribution checks and Appendices E-F's expanded-search sensitivity and weight-grouping tests are absent; the original main-text inter-sample similarity plot is retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for performance results. The retained analysis across 100 input samples concerns activation-parameter similarity, rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains baseline scores but replaces proposed-method results: W4A4 SAM-B/Faster R-CNN changes from 11.7 to 17.9 mAP, and SAM-L/DINO from 36.6 to 40.2, alongside method and calibration revisions. SAM2 results are added and ImageNet results removed. Hardware speedup/efficiency ratios change from 7.89/8.64 to 7.12/6.62 under different platforms and workloads, so these do not establish a regression. v4 also contains an unresolved CondiQuant score conflict: 0.3 in Section 4.3.4 versus 3.8 in Figure 12.

T1.justification: v4 adds a condition-number error bound and substantial ACNR mathematical development: a regularized objective, proximal subproblems, a fixed-singular-vector restriction, closed-form spectral updates, and energy preservation (Equations 5 and 7-13). LNQ introduces a nonlinear transformation, its inverse, and an initialization objective (Equations 17-19). The earlier HLUQ mathematics remains substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contribution expands from addressing two activation-distribution challenges with HLUQ/CAG to addressing four challenges with ACNR/HLUQ/CAG/LNQ. Abstract, introduction, and conclusion add SAM2 video-quantization benchmarking and associated performance claims. v2's explicit claim of being the first to enable 4-bit SAM PTQ is omitted, and the headline accuracy and hardware claims are revised.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations involving directional activation noise, weight conditioning, spectral preservation, and heterogeneous attention distributions, plus an overfitting interpretation for CondiQuant's results. Component interpretations shift toward four-component cooperation. v2's explicit limitation deferring CPU/GPU deployment is removed, together with the supplementary interpretations about parameter-search insensitivity, weight-grouping generalization, and why CAG is unnecessary for the evaluated DeiT adaptation.

D1.justification: v4 newly specifies a 4e-5 learning rate, cosine scheduling, batch size one, and ACNR/LNQ hyperparameters. It revises hardware documentation to describe Zynq processing-system/programmed-logic partitioning, Vitis HLS operations, and LNQ lookup-table storage. These disclosures accompany the changed hardware evaluation. The advertised code location changes from Keio-CSG/AHCPTQ to Wenlun-Zhang/AHCQ-SAM.

R1.justification: Related work expands into separate efficient-SAM and PTQ discussions, covering distillation, pruning, caching, and additional quantization research. CondiQuant becomes a central methodological reference against which ACNR is positioned. SAQ-SAM and newer video-SAM work are introduced, while PQ-SAM, already cited in v2, receives substantive discussion rather than merely another citation.

P1.justification: The paper is extensively reorganized into a journal-style narrative. The title and framework name change, challenges are integrated into component-specific Challenge/Solution subsections, related work is subdivided, and hardware and qualitative material are incorporated into the main text. The separate supplement and limitations section disappear, while authorship information and biographies expand.

P2.justification: Figure 1 expands from two challenges to four, and a new four-component overview accompanies separate HLUQ/CAG diagrams. Tables gain explicit floating-point columns and a new video-results table; hardware displays and qualitative examples are replaced. Numerous supplementary plots and tables disappear. These substantial display changes accompany the journal layout, beyond renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: The strongest gain is substantially better support for practical deployment: v2 validates only a decoder MLP block, whereas v4 reports SAM-B frame rates and resource use in Section 4.5 and Table 4. ACNR/LNQ derivations and targeted ablations also deepen the technical justification, while video experiments test materially broader applicability. These gains outweigh the loss of earlier sensitivity evidence. Reporting quality remains imperfect: Tables 1-2 contain TODO method labels, and the CondiQuant prose conflicts with Figure 12, weakening confidence in that particular comparison.
